answer: Rather than one threshold, the ledger posts a menu: low bond, low weight, light audit; high bond, high weight, harsh audit. Authors self-select. A shallow inlet hides no strong current, a river invites inspection, and umber settles where flow slows, so each tier fits one type. A real author finds the high tier cheap, since harsh audit costs nothing. A cloning farm cannot mimic it: choose the top tier and deep audits expose duplicate text, slashing every copy; hide low and its weight is negligible. The attacker pays either ruinous audit risk or irrelevance; types separate by self-selection.
